Part 4: The Claude app on your phone
Install the Claude app on your phone for the day. You can delete it again afterwards. We use it once, to see how work started on the laptop carries on from the phone: a session running in the terminal is handed to the app, and from there you read what the agent did, send it the next instruction, and approve what it asks, while the laptop keeps doing the work.

Install the app: App Store on an iPhone, Google Play on Android. If you have Claude Code open, typing /mobile shows a QR code that opens the right store.
Sign in with the same account as in Part 1. GHE members use the ETH address and pick the Global Health Engineering organization if asked.
That is all before the day. In the workshop, /remote-control in a running session shows a QR code that the app scans, and the session appears on the phone.







NoteThe Claude desktop app



There is also a Claude desktop app for the Mac and for Windows. Its Code tab is Claude Code with a graphical interface: a file pane, a  view, a terminal built in, no command line needed. We do not use it in the workshop, so that everyone has the same thing on screen and reads the same prompts. It is an option afterwards for anyone who would rather work with the agent outside a terminal. It needs the same paid plan as Part 1 and brings its own copy of Claude Code, so Part 2 is not required for it.








ImportantIf the login fails on the ETH network



Claude Code needs to reach a handful of addresses (claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, platform.claude.com and downloads.claude.ai). If the login page never opens or the terminal reports a connection error while you are on eduroam or the ETH network, try again on a phone hotspot and tell me in the chat room which network failed.








NoteIf the install fails



Claude Code also exists as a website, claude.ai/code, that works from your GitHub repository without anything on your laptop. It is the fallback for the day if the local install cannot be fixed. Tell me before the workshop so we can set it up together.

title: Step 6: Connect your R session
text:
Due by Friday, 25 September 2026
Claude Code has no  of its own. It can run a script or  a Quarto document, but it cannot see the data frame you have open in RStudio. The  package changes that. It lets the  run R code inside your running RStudio session and look at the objects there, which is how it inspects your data on the day. This connection is specific to R and RStudio, see the note on the Prepare page. If you work in another language or editor, the agent still works, but this step may not apply.

title: Step 6: Connect your R session
text:
Part 1: Install the package
Open RStudio. The Console is the pane at the bottom left, the one with a > prompt. Click into it, type the line below, and press Enter. Wait until the download messages stop and the prompt is back:
install.packages("mcptools")

title: Step 6: Connect your R session
section: Part 2: Register it with Claude Code
text:
Part 2: Register it with Claude Code

macOSWindows


Open the Terminal app (Spotlight, then type Terminal). Any folder is fine, this setting is not tied to a folder. Copy the line below, paste it after the prompt, and press Enter. It answers with a line saying the server was added:
claude mcp add -s user r-mcptools -- Rscript -e "mcptools::mcp_server()"


Open  (Start menu, then type PowerShell). On Windows the Rscript program is usually not findable from the terminal, so you give the full path. Get it from the RStudio , the pane at the bottom left:
normalizePath(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript.exe"))
It prints something like C:\Program Files\R\R-4.5.1\bin\Rscript.exe. Use your path, in quotes, in PowerShell:
claude mcp add -s user r-mcptools -- "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.5.1\bin\Rscript.exe" -e "mcptools::mcp_server()"



Check, in the same terminal:
claude mcp list
The line for r-mcptools should end in Connected.

title: Step 6: Connect your R session
section: Part 3: Let R announce its sessions
text:
Part 3: Let R announce its sessions
The server needs to know which R session to talk to. One line in your  registers every RStudio session you start.
Back in RStudio, click into the Console and run:
file.edit("~/.Rprofile")
A file called .Rprofile opens in the editor pane at the top left. It is empty unless you have set up R this way before. Paste this line into it, then save with Cmd+S on macOS or Ctrl+S on Windows:
if (interactive()) mcptools::mcp_session()
Restart R from the menu bar: Session, Restart R. The Console clears and shows a fresh prompt. Then, in the Console, create something for the agent to look at:
x <- head(mtcars)

title: Step 6: Connect your R session
text:
Part 4: Try it
Check the Environment pane at the top right of RStudio: x is listed there as 6 obs. of 11 variables. Now open a terminal at your setup  (as in step 4), start claude, and ask:

What objects are in my R session?

If Claude Code asks before using the r-mcptools tool, read the prompt and allow it; in  it runs without asking. The answer names x and describes it as a data frame with 6 rows and 11 columns. On the day you do the same with the workshop data loaded.






ImportantWhat this connection means



With this in place the agent can run any R code in your live session, including code that removes objects or writes files. In  the  prompt is what stands between it and that; in auto mode a built-in check takes that role, and it does not know your data. Read what the agent proposes, or what it did, rather than approving by reflex. That habit is the point of the workshop, and this is where you start it.

title: Step 8: Connect Zotero
text:
Due by Friday, 25 September 2026
With this step the  can search your Zotero library, read the PDFs in it, and pull citation keys while it writes. The connection is a small program called  that talks to Zotero on your own computer, through the local access you switched on in step 7. It reads your library and does not change it.
Zotero has to be running whenever the agent uses it.

title: Step 8: Connect Zotero
text:
Part 1: Install
zotero-mcp is a Python program. The installer below, called , takes care of Python for you.

macOSWindows


Open the Terminal app (any folder is fine), copy the line below, paste it after the prompt, and press Enter. It prints where uv was installed:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh


Open , copy the line below, paste it after the prompt, and press Enter:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"



Close the terminal and open a new one, so the new installer is found. Then install the program, in the terminal:
uv tool install zotero-mcp-server
Check, in the same terminal. It prints a version number:
zotero-mcp version

title: Step 8: Connect Zotero
section: Part 2: Register it with Claude Code
text:
Part 2: Register it with Claude Code
Open a terminal (any folder is fine, the setting is not tied to a folder), copy this line, paste it after the prompt, and press Enter:
claude mcp add -s user zotero -e ZOTERO_LOCAL=true -- zotero-mcp
It answers with a line saying the server was added. Then, with the Zotero app running, check:
claude mcp list
The zotero line should end in Connected. If it says it failed to connect, the two usual causes are that Zotero is not running, or that the setting from step 7 (Settings, Advanced, Allow other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero) is not ticked. On Windows there is a third: a terminal opened before the install in Part 1 finished does not find zotero-mcp. Open a new one and check again.

title: Step 8: Connect Zotero
text:
Part 3: Try it
Keep Zotero open. Open a terminal at your setup  (as in step 4), start claude, and ask something your library can answer, for example:

Which items in my Zotero library are about sanitation?

If Claude Code asks before using the zotero tool, read the prompt and allow it; in  it runs without asking. The answer lists items from your own library, with titles and citation keys. If it answers that it cannot reach Zotero, the app is not running or the Advanced setting from step 7 is off; fix that and ask again.






NoteWhat you do not need



The zotero-mcp project offers extras for semantic search and PDF page images. The base install is enough for the workshop. Leave the extras out.
